findings.claim: classify_late_fee_tier is currently defined at demo-repo/src/loanflow/late_fee_tier.py:21-28. Its first statement is the negative check (`if days_past_due < 0: raise ValidationError("days_past_due must not be negative")`). It then returns "grace" when days_past_due <= 5, "standard" when days_past_due < 30, and "severe" otherwise. The function has no type check, so a float or bool goes straight into the comparisons. For example, 10.5 returns "standard" and True (== 1) returns "grace".
late_fee_tier.py imports ValidationError at module level with `from loanflow.errors import ValidationError`. ValidationError is defined in loanflow/errors.py as a subclass of LoanflowError.

The repository's integer-guard idiom `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)` raising ValidationError appears in exactly three places in demo-repo: classify_credit_score (risk_bands.py:46-47), Money.__post_init__ (primitives.py:24-25) and Percentage.__post_init__ (primitives.py:54-55). Where a range check exists, the type check comes before it: risk_bands.py:46 is before the 300-850 check at :48, and primitives.py:54 is before the negative check at :56. Each error message has the form '<name> must be an integer ...'.

Existing pytest.raises(ValidationError) regression tests cover the guard idiom. test_credit_score_non_integer_and_bool_is_rejected covers 700.5, 700.0, True and False. test_percentage_rejects_non_integer_and_bool_basis_points covers 1.5, True and False. test_money_rejects_non_integer_cents covers only the float 1.5; no Money(True) or Money(False) test exists.

demo-repo/tests/unit/test_late_fee_tier.py has two tests. test_late_fee_tier_boundaries checks 0 and 5 -> grace, 6 and 29 -> standard, 30 and 31 -> severe. test_negative_days_past_due_is_rejected checks that -1 raises ValidationError. No test passes a float or bool. The file already imports pytest and ValidationError.

demo-repo/tests/unit/test_late_fee_tier_regression.py is a pre-existing, disclosed fixture that is out of scope. It asserts classify_late_fee_tier(30) == "severe" and classify_late_fee_tier(29) == "standard", and uses only plain ints.

No production code calls classify_late_fee_tier, so no production caller passes a non-int days_past_due. Across demo-repo, only late_fee_tier.py (the definition), the two late-fee test files and docs/late-fee-tier-policy.md contain 'late_fee'. In .py files, the only references to classify_late_fee_tier are the definition and the test call sites, and every test call site passes a plain int.

findings.claim: Adding the guard is unlikely to break anything in the repository. Both late-fee test files pass only plain ints, and no production caller exists. The only intended behavior change is for non-int input.
findings.reasoning: F-5 and F-6 show that every existing call to classify_late_fee_tier passes a plain int, and F-7 (a not_found check, noted here only as context) found no production callers. A bool/int guard rejects only bool and non-int values (F-3 idiom), so none of the existing calls would be affected. AC-3's preservation of the -1 rejection holds as long as the guard comes before the existing negative check at F-1's line 22, because -1 is a plain int and passes the guard.

findings.claim: The repository corroborates the Obsidian note 'Engineering Notes/loanflow-integer-input-convention.md' (LFCONV-INTGUARD-01). The note's idiom, its bool-before-int order, its three locations (Money.__post_init__, Percentage.__post_init__, classify_credit_score), its use of loanflow.errors.ValidationError, and its type-check-before-range-check rule all match current code. One small difference: the note says each guard has its own pytest.raises(ValidationError) regression test, but the Money guard's test covers only a float, with no bool case. late_fee_tier.py currently does not follow the convention, which matches the defect the scope describes. This finding rests on the repository citations. The retained read-evidence file is cited only as metadata for where the claim came from.
